item.title: Nation further opens up vast mkt to imports
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
China is pressing ahead with efforts to expand imports, positioning its vast domestic market as an anchor of global demand and a rare source of certainty for overseas businesses as protectionist headwinds and geopolitical tensions roil international trade, government officials and experts said. Expanding imports is a high priority for China, said Li Chenggang, China's international trade representative and vice-minister of commerce, noting that the country has remained the world's second-largest import market for 17 consecutive years and contributed to global trade growth. Li made the remarks at an international symposium on the Export-to-China Capacity Development Report in Geneva on Wednesday, calling on trading partners to seize opportunities under the "Big Market for All: Export to China" initiative. Launched in Shanghai in November 2025, the initiative was conceived from the perspective of China's trading partners and represents a proactive step to help them expand exports to China, Li said. The initiative aims to create more opportunities for the world through China's own development, while strengthening collective efforts to uphold multilateralism and free trade, and address development challenges, he added. China's growing appetite for imports is giving substance to its pledge to share market opportunities with the world, with goods imports rising 23.6 percent year-on-year to 18.82 trillion yuan ($2.82 trillion) in the first 10 months, outpacing the 17.6 percent gain in exports, according to the General Administration of Customs. "The Chinese market is an anchor of resilience for the global economy," said Wang Xuekun, head of the Chinese Academy of International Trade and Economic Cooperation. For global businesses, the opportunity lies in the combination of China's market scale and its evolving consumer needs, Wang said, pointing to the world's largest middle-income population, and consumer and import markets that both rank among the world's two largest. As consumption becomes more sophisticated, China is unlocking fresh demand and creating new opportunities for investment, he added. Li, China's international trade representative, said holding the symposium in Geneva as China marks 25 years of World Trade Organization membership reaffirmed the country's confidence and resolve to keep expanding imports. China will carry that message to Zurich on Thursday, where the Ministry of Commerce and the Swiss-Chinese Chamber of Commerce will jointly host an "Export to China" event to help Swiss businesses tap the Chinese market. The outreach builds on substantial commercial ties. China is already Switzerland's largest trading partner in Asia, while bilateral trade surged 127 percent year-on-year to $89 billion in the first nine months of 2026, according to the Ministry of Commerce. The strong trade figures come as the two countries seek to turn their complementary economic strengths into broader opportunities through deeper market opening, with the Zurich event taking place nearly a month after they signed a protocol to upgrade their free trade agreement in Beijing in late October. Under the upgraded agreement, zero-tariff treatment will ultimately cover more than 99 percent of bilateral goods trade, while further opening in services and investment will give businesses greater access to each other's markets, the ministry said. That wider opening promises fresh opportunities for Swiss companies already betting on the Chinese market's long-term potential. "China is one of our most important markets in the world and is strategically important for our international business," said Rick Kozloski, president of the China unit of Swiss eye care company Alcon. Patients' growing expectations for better vision after treatment are sustaining demand for increasingly sophisticated eye care products and services, he said. zhangchenxu@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Paws in vogue: dressing pampered pets in period finery
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
Liuliu's wardrobe can put many fashionistas to shame. She owns dozens of traditional Chinese outfits — from flowing skirts to elaborate cloud-collared hanfu — and even gets personal fittings whenever a new design comes off the sewing table. The mixed British Shorthair cat is the star model of Chunfeng Daxiaoqiao, an online shop specializing in traditional Chinese clothing for pets. The shop's 32-year-old founder, who goes by the name Qiu Qiao, designs every outfit herself — drawing inspiration from China's cultural heritage — and makes sure comfort comes first. If Liuliu cannot move freely in an outfit, it will not be offered for sale, she said. "Pets are family to me. They are a responsibility. I want to protect them and give them the best life possible, because they bring me happiness and companionship," Qiu Qiao added. At her shop, traditional Chinese outfits such as the mamianqun (horse-face skirt) and yunjian (cloud-shaped collar) have been reimagined for four-legged customers, with every piece of clothing tailored to allow them to walk, sit and play uninhibitedly. "We want people to recognize the cultural characteristics of traditional Chinese clothing while ensuring that the outfits remain comfortable for pets to wear," Qiu Qiao said. Her very first original design, titled When the Lychees Are Ripe, was inspired by Yang Yuhuan — better known as Yang Guifei — the celebrated consort of Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang Dynasty (618-907) and one of the Four Beauties in China. Taking this as a starting point, some of her collections draw on the legendary beauties, translating historical imagery into elaborate pet costumes. The Chunfeng Daxiaoqiao brand name also carries a literary echo, drawing inspiration from a line by the Southern Song Dynasty (1127-1279) poet Xin Qiji about the legendary beauty of the two Qiao sisters. Qiu Qiao's entrepreneurial journey began when she became disillusioned with office life in Beijing and Qingdao, Shandong province. In 2019, after rescuing a stray kitten, she decided to combine her love of animals with her interest in traditional Chinese culture. She quit her job, returned to her hometown in Hunan province, and launched the online business — with her cat Liuliu as its first model. "In the past, pet clothing was largely about keeping animals warm or providing basic protection. Today, consumers are also looking for distinctive designs, quality materials and outfits that reflect their own tastes," she said. Pet birthdays, weddings and themed photo shoots have created further demand, as owners increasingly see clothing as a way to celebrate their furry companions and create lasting memories. For Liu Yaoru, another pet entrepreneur, the opportunity came from a different problem — finding clothes that actually fit her greyhound's slender frame. She turned to her family's clothing business for women and asked factory tailors to make outfits for her dog based on her own designs. "I posted some photos of my dog wearing these clothes on Xiaohongshu. I didn't expect so many people to ask where they could get the same outfits, or whether I could make something similar for their dogs," Liu recalled. As word spread on social media and elsewhere, orders poured in. Liu now also offers upcycling, turning owners' unwanted clothing into new outfits for their pets. The trend reflects the expansion of China's pet economy. According to data highlighted in March at the 6th China Pet Industry Development Conference in Beijing, the nation's pet consumption market reached 312.6 billion yuan ($47 billion) by the end of 2025, up 4.1 percent year-on-year. The pet clothing sector has emerged as a fast-growing market, with its value rising from 3.58 billion yuan in 2020 to 12.95 billion yuan in 2025, with an annual growth rate of more than 35 percent in overseas sales. item.title: Moon rocks a symbol of China's global vision
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
One of the most memorable advertising tag lines in the United States was "You've come a long way, baby". The phrase can also be used to describe China's meteoric rise in the past few decades. Nothing proves this point better than a recent ceremony at the United Nations headquarters in Vienna, Austria, where China presented moon rocks and soil samples from the far side of the Moon for permanent display. The out-of-this-world gift has transformed China's scientific achievement into a lasting diplomatic symbol at the heart of multilateralism. The Chang'e-6 lunar mission returned to Earth with almost two kilograms of lunar material in June 2024, marking the first and only successful retrieval of samples from the Moon's far side. The complex mission required advanced robotics, autonomous spacecraft operations and a relay satellite to communicate with Earth despite the Moon blocking direct radio contact. The samples are both a unique scientific treasure and evidence of China's advancing technological capabilities. At the Vienna ceremony, Shan Zhongde, the administrator of the China National Space Administration, emphasized China's commitment to sharing the benefits of space exploration internationally and promoting peaceful use of space. Monica Juma, director-general of the UN Office at Vienna, highlighted the connection between scientific achievement and international cooperation, underscoring Vienna's role as a world capital where science and diplomacy meet. Aarti Holla-Maini, director of the UN Office for Outer Space Affairs, noted that the gift serves as a teacher, not a trophy, emphasizing that the rare lunar samples from the far side, thanks to China, belong to everyone. Li Song, China's permanent representative to the UN and other international organizations in Vienna, also shared his views during an interview at the event. He said that the event demonstrates China's commitment and actions to firmly uphold the status and role of the UN in collaboration with all parties, improve global governance of outer space and better benefit all of humanity. Together, these remarks framed the samples not merely as a national prize, but as an invitation for all nations to participate in humanity's exploration of the universe. The ceremony reminded me of a historical parallel that underscores China's remarkable journey. In the early 15th century, admiral Zheng He of the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644) led treasure ships across the Indian Ocean, carrying envoys and gifts to foreign rulers. Some experts even suggest that Zheng visited the Americas before Christopher Columbus and circumnavigated the globe a century before Ferdinand Magellan. Six centuries ago, Zheng's fabled voyages projected Chinese maritime power, cultivated diplomatic relationships and brought extraordinary objects, such as giraffes from East Africa, back to China. These were seen as auspicious Chinese unicorns or qilin, symbolizing the prestige of Zheng's diplomatic exchanges. The underlying diplomatic mechanism resonates through the ages. Just as in the past, China's contemporary achievements have produced extraordinary objects that communicate capability and prestige. Zheng's treasure fleet was part of the message. Today, the Chang'e missions are the 21st century equivalent, with lunar samples serving as extraordinary objects from a quarter-million-mile journey. But there is a striking difference. Zheng demonstrated China's ability to reach distant parts of the known world, while Chang'e-6 demonstrated its ability to retrieve material from an unexplored region of another world. The frontiers of discovery have shifted from the Earth's oceans to the Moon's surface and beyond. Retrieving lunar material requires advanced launch systems, robotics, communications and autonomous operations. The samples convey two messages: China's capabilities and its willingness to share a finite, precious resource with the international community. The Vienna display serves as a permanent reminder that an achievement of one country can become a shared interest. It also demonstrates how a small quantity of material can carry diplomatic significance far beyond its physical size. This gift to the UN in Vienna also embodies China's commitment to a community with a shared future for humanity. From Zheng's treasure fleets to Chang'e's journey to the Moon's far side, the principle remains the same: extraordinary achievements can open diplomatic doors. The Chang'e-6 lunar samples gifted to the UN serve as more than symbols of China's scientific achievement. They also echo the spirit of the Global Development, Global Security, Global Civilization and Global Governance Initiatives — reminding us that humanity's greatest achievements are those that expand our shared horizons, transcend national boundaries and benefit all humanity. China's out-of-this-world win-win space diplomacy continues to reach new heights with the successful Nov 25 launch of the Shenzhou XXIV spaceflight mission. It marks the participation of the first foreign astronaut aboard the Tiangong space station, Pakistani Muhammad Zeeshan Ali. The author is a senior fellow at the Center for China and Globalization. The views don't necessarily reflect those of China Daily. item.title: Xi hails China-Pakistan milestone
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
President Xi Jinping said on Wednesday that the joint space exploration by astronauts from China and Pakistan is a vivid embodiment of the deep-rooted friendship between the two countries. It marks another important achievement in bilateral cooperation, Xi said while exchanging congratulations with Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari on the joint spaceflight mission. In the message, Xi said that he was glad to learn of a Pakistani astronaut's successful entry into space aboard a Chinese spaceship for the first time, making him the first foreign astronaut to visit China's Tiangong space station. Xi extended his warm congratulations to the Pakistani government and people, as well as to astronauts and space professionals from both countries on behalf of the Chinese government and people. He noted that China and Pakistan are all-weather strategic cooperative partners, saying that the friendship between the two countries has remained rock-solid and unbreakable since diplomatic ties were established 75 years ago. Emphasizing that China's space station is an ark of peace, friendship and cooperation, Xi said that China stands ready to work with Pakistan and other countries to advance the peaceful use of outer space, deepen international space cooperation and improve global governance in outer space, to ensure that outer space exploration delivers greater benefits to humanity. Zardari expressed profound appreciation to the Chinese government and the brotherly Chinese people on behalf of the Pakistani government and people. He said the historic space cooperation between Pakistan and China and the first Pakistani astronaut entering China's space station come as the two countries commemorate the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations. Such cooperation demonstrates China's remarkable progress in space science and technology, its firm commitment to the peaceful use of outer space, and the significance of building a community with a shared future for humanity, Zardari said, adding that it will further strengthen bilateral friendship and promote the two countries' all-weather strategic cooperative partnership to a higher level.

item.title: Snow holidays see school kids hit ski slopes
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
Children with skis slung over their shoulders boarded free shuttle buses at Chongli's South Passenger Transport Hub and headed for the nearby slopes as Zhangjiakou, Hebei province, rolled out its first school snow holiday recently. "I used to watch skiing on TV, but now I can try it myself," said Wang Ting, a student from Zhuolu county, who tried skiing at Snow Ruyi Ski Resort. Zhangjiakou has arranged a three-day break for students from first to eighth grade. Primary school pupils had their holiday from Nov 18 to 20, while students in the seventh and eighth grades are scheduled to take theirs from Nov 25 to 27. Local authorities are encouraging employers to offer flexible leave and prioritize schedule adjustments for workers with younger children. Zhang Litao, a staff member at the Nanzhan subdistrict office, said he had secured leave from work and booked a Wednesday skiing trip to a ski resort for his eighth grade child, who has been skiing for years. To make skiing more accessible, local authorities and businesses have paired the holidays with free transportation, discounted services and access to selected cultural venues. Four Chongli ski resorts — Fulong, Yinhe, Snow Ruyi and Duolemeidi — are offering a combined 650 free skiing admissions per day for local students. At Snow Ruyi, students can receive free ski passes and equipment, while accompanying parents can get 30 percent discounts, plus 15 percent off on accommodation. Students pay a 20 yuan insurance fee ($3), said Sun Yan, the resort's brand manager. Safety is a priority. The city's education bureau instructed schools to provide preholiday safety education on winter sports and traffic, and to coordinate with parents on supervision. Schools were also asked to provide care for students who need supervision during the break. At Fulong, staff members set aside beginner areas, prepared equipment in advance and arranged lessons covering safe skiing and basic techniques. About 100 children signed up to ski at Snow Ruyi on the opening day, most of them accompanied by family members, Hebei Daily reported. Fulong staff reported that visitor numbers were up about 30 percent year-on-year after the break began. Similar holidays were tried last winter in Urumqi and Altay of the Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region, in Jilin province and later in Hulunbuir, Inner Mongolia. This year, all these places have renewed or refined their arrangements, with many breaks extended to five days by linking them with adjacent weekends. In Altay, the Dec 16-18 holiday will involve four ski resorts and public venues, as well as study tours and cultural activities. Local tourism businesses are developing dedicated skiing and study tour packages for the holiday. The Keketuohai Study Tour Camp, operated by a State-owned tourism company, has introduced separate three — and five-day skiing programs and study tours covering local history, geology, ecology and ethnic culture. "The programs are open to local families and visitors from outside the region," said Nana, a teacher at the camp. In Jilin, bookings for ice-and-snow destinations rose more than 120 percent from the previous period ahead of the December break, according to Tongcheng Travel, as reported by Cailian News. The province is encouraging employers to accommodate parents' existing paid leave or flexible time off. The initiatives draw on national education guidance that allows local authorities to arrange school calendars while maintaining required teaching hours. A 2024 State Council guideline set a target of 1.2 trillion yuan for the ice-and-snow economy by 2027. In Chongli, a 2022 Beijing Winter Olympics host, around 30,000 residents work directly or indirectly in winter sports and tourism, Hebei Daily reported. Liu Fan, an associate professor at the Communication University of China, told Guangming Daily that snow holidays offer more time for winter activities by extending consumption beyond ski resorts to accommodation, dining and cultural products.

item.title: 'Auntie Basketball' team scores cultural points on US tour
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
'Auntie Basketball' team scores cultural points on US tour Guizhou's community-based players use sport to foster exchanges By LIU BOQIAN and YANG JUN in Guiyang | China Daily Updated: 2026-11-26 09:07 Share - WeChat Players from two "Auntie Basketball" teams compete in the championship battle in Danjiang town, Leishan county, Guizhou province, on Aug 9. The county-level "Village Cup" women's basketball league concluded after nearly two months of competition, featuring 33 village teams from nine towns and drawing thousands of visitors to the area. LIANG WEN/FOR CHINA DAILY Loud cheers and applause echoed through the gymnasium at Crimson Cliffs High School in Washington City, Utah, as a group of women from Guizhou province faced the school's girls' basketball team in a friendly match during a recent trip to the United States. Yang Xiaohui (left), a member from the delegation, talks in Mandarin with students from Crimson Cliffs High School in Washington City, Utah, on Oct 2. CHINA DAILY The visitors were members of the "Auntie Basketball" delegation, a grassroots women's basketball team from Qiandongnan Miao and Dong autonomous prefecture in Guizhou. More than 20 members of the delegation traveled to various communities from Sept 28 to Oct 6, visiting states, including California, Nevada, and Utah.

item.title: MND releases video urging Japan to fulfill chemical weapons obligations
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-26
On Nov 24, China's Ministry of National Defense (MND) released the fifth episode of its video series Japan's Abandoned Chemical Weapons in China on its X account, @MND_China. Titled An Obligation Japan Must Fulfill, the video highlights the unfinished task of destroying chemical weapons abandoned by Japan in China. It revisits the 30th session of the Conference of the States Parties to the Chemical Weapons Convention and features remarks by Fernando Arias González, then director-general of the Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW), and a passage from Japanese historian Yoshimi Yoshiaki's book Dokugasusen to Nihongun. The video emphasizes that a world free of chemical weapons cannot be achieved until all chemical weapons abandoned by Japan in China have been destroyed. It also calls on Japan to fulfill its international obligations. Video source: Ministry of National Defense

item.title: What will shape the China-US AI future? | Short documentary
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
The US is betting big on AI. Tech giants are pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into chips, data centers, and power — all to build the world's most advanced models and keep their weights closed. But China's open-weight breakthroughs are challenging that playbook. From DeepSeek to Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, Chinese developers are closing the gap at a fraction of the cost and releasing the weights of the world's leading models for developers worldwide to build on. Open versus closed is more than a technical choice. It represents two different paths for AI's future. Will AI concentrate power in a few hands or give more countries the tools to shape their own futures? Join MediaUnlocked for more insights.

item.title: Shenzhou crews at a glance
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
The Shenzhou XXIV crewed spaceship blasted off from Jiuquan on Wednesday morning and successfully entered orbit, carrying Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali to China's Tiangong space station. The mission marks the first joint flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program, and the first time a foreign astronaut has visited the Tiangong space station.
